newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany sees drop in racist arson attacks in 1996. [CORRECTED 23:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Germany sees drop in racist arson attacks in 1996. [CORRECTED 23:50 GMT]

text.p: The German Federal Criminal Office on Monday reported a drop in racially-motivated arson attacks on asylum homes and foreigners' accommodation in 1996.
The office said in a reply to a parliamentary question that 14 such attacks had been registered in 1996, seven of which had been cleared up.

Although the Criminal Office could not provide comparative figures, the Federal Office for Protection of the Constitution (BfV) said the number of such attacks had peaked in 1992 at 656 attacks and had fallen steadily since, reaching 37 in 1995 (corrects from "last year").
The office said the total number of racist attacks in Germany had also declined over the last few years, dropping to 540 in 1995 from a high of 2,277 in 1992.
BfV spokesman Hans-Gert Langer attributed the fall to the fact that authorities had clamped down on racist violence and that it was increasingly unacceptable in German society.
"Society has decided to distance itself from such right-wing extremism," Langer said.
Germany suffered a wave of racist violence following unification in 1990, particularly in the economically backward, formerly communist east where asylum homes were often a target.
